Inlinr engineering lifecycle

A specific map of the workflows we built into this repository. Discovery, intake, build, PR gates, and release sit on the top strip. The monitoring strategy gets its own loop because it is unusual: three dedicated agents maintain the readable monitoring scenarios, the machine-readable contract, and the runtime telemetry, and a deterministic pipeline turns that contract into validated Azure alerts.

Discovery Intake Build PR gates Release Monitoring loop

Reading guide

Start with the high-level lifecycle strip right below — it shows how work moves from discovery to release. The monitoring strategy panel then covers the parallel loop that keeps scenarios, contract, telemetry, and alerts aligned. The workflow catalog lists every named workflow grouped by phase, with the input each one consumes and the output it produces.

High-level lifecycle

Discovery agents file issues. Issue Triage routes them. Implementation produces a reviewable pull request. Three specialized review agents plus CI decide merge readiness. Release packages, deploys monitoring, and publishes to the Marketplace.

Monitoring strategy

Inlinr's monitoring is layered intentionally. Three agentic workflows maintain the readable scenario catalog, the canonical machine contract, and the runtime telemetry implementation. A separate deterministic pipeline validates that contract and generates alert policies, and the release workflow deploys them to Azure. Each layer has a single source of truth and a clear writer.

Discovery

Agents that find the next high-leverage work and file it as issues.

Head of Product

DailyAgentic

Product strategy lead. Reviews repo, market, and adjacent AI workflows to file high-leverage product issues.

In
Repo activity, product/, market and adjacent-AI signals.
Out
One bounded product issue per run.

UX Review

Twice weeklyAgentic

UX design lead. Audits editor-native fit, motion, and perceived speed. Files distinct UX issues only.

In
product/, architecture/, specs/, src/, media/, package.json, plus VS Code UX docs and Marketplace references.
Out

Spec Librarian

DailyAgentic

Audits drift across product, architecture, specs, monitoring, and shipped code. Opens at most one drift issue.

In
product/, architecture/, specs/, src/, monitoring/.
Out
One drift issue with the specific divergence.

Intake

Bound and route each piece of work before any code is written.

Issue Triage

On issueAgentic

Classifies issues, applies routing labels, posts a single triage comment, and assigns Copilot only when work is bounded and low-risk.

In
New or updated issue body and metadata.
Out
Routing labels, one triage comment, and optional Copilot assignment.

Build

Local-first spec, implement, and verify loop. Tests run before any PR opens.

Spec Kit (specify, plan, tasks, implement)

Per sliceHybrid

Local-first authoring flow that turns approved scenarios into implementation-ready specs, plans, and ordered tasks.

In
Approved scenario, product/, architecture/.
Out
spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md, source code.

Mocha unit tests

Local + CIDeterministic

Pure-Node unit suite under tests/unit driven by @vscode/test-cli through tests/runTest.ts. Runs via npm run test:unit.

In
src/ + tests/unit.
Out
Pass/fail report on logic and contracts.

Mocha integration tests

Local + CIDeterministic

Runs in a real VS Code Extension Host via @vscode/test-electron. Exercises commands, custom editors, and provider wiring under tests/integration.

In
Compiled extension + tests/integration in Extension Host.
Out
Pass/fail report on commands and providers.

Playwright webview tests

Local + CIDeterministic

Browser-based selection contract tests per ADR-007. Runs the Markdown viewer bundle in headless Chromium under tests/webview via npm run test:webview.

In
media/markdownViewer/ bundle + selection fixtures.
Out
Selection-geometry pass/fail + trace artifacts.

verify:release harness

Pre-PR + releaseDeterministic

One-shot gate that compiles, runs the full Mocha suite, and packages the VSIX. Mirrors what CI and the release workflow run.

In
Working tree.
Out
Packaged .vsix + test evidence.

PR gates

Parallel agentic reviews plus CI decide whether auto-merge can fire.

Practicality Review

On PRAgentic

Surfaces reality gaps, hidden assumptions, silent failures, and loops that are not actually closed.

In
PR diff, product/user-scenarios.md, scenario context.
Out
Review comments + clearance label.

PR Security Review

On PRAgentic

Checks XSS, prompt injection, telemetry leakage, workflow privilege drift, and protected paths.

In
PR diff, workflow files, architecture/security-principles.md.
Out
Review comments + clearance label.

PR Maintainability Review

On PRAgentic

Flags layer violations, duplicated rules, weak tests, and design drift that raises future change cost.

In
PR diff + architecture/ principles and contracts.
Out
Review comments + clearance label.

CI

On PR + mainDeterministic

Compiles, runs unit and integration suites, and packages the VSIX artifact for inspection.

In
PR commit.
Out
Build + test status, .vsix artifact.

PR Auto-merge Enabler

On review runDeterministic

Enables auto-merge only when all three review labels are cleared and no protected paths are touched.

In
Three review-clearance labels + workflow_run.
Out
Auto-merge enabled on the PR.

Repository structure

The harness only works when each workflow knows where to read intent from and where to write evidence to. These are the top-level folders the lifecycle relies on, grouped by the role they play. Source-of-truth folders are written by humans (or by agents that maintain a canonical artifact); implementation and operations folders are where code, tests, and pipelines apply that intent.

Source of truth

Human-authored intent. Agents read these to decide what to build, review, monitor, and ship.

product/

Human-authored product intent. Read first by every planning and review agent.

  • Product outline
  • User scenarios
  • Non-goals
  • UX principles
  • Glossary
  • Development workflow
  • Markdown presentation roadmap
architecture/

Technical source of truth for system shape and decisions.

  • High-level architecture
  • Engineering principles
  • Security principles
  • Data-contract rules
  • ADRs
specs/

SpecKit feature specs that drive the build phase.

  • Spec (spec.md)
  • Plan (plan.md)
  • Tasks (tasks.md)
  • Data model
  • Contracts
  • Checklists
  • Quickstart
monitoring/

Scenario and telemetry source of truth that drives the monitoring loop.

  • Monitoring scenarios catalog
  • Scenario contract (canonical YAML)
  • Alert policies
  • Telemetry guidelines

Implementation

Where intent becomes runnable code and where tests prove it still matches intent.

src/

VS Code extension TypeScript, organized by surface.

  • Commands
  • Editors
  • Presentation
  • Rendering
  • Requests
  • Sessions
  • Telemetry
  • Webview
  • Onboarding
  • Extension entry point
media/

Webview assets shipped with the extension.

  • Markdown viewer scripts
  • Markdown viewer styles
tests/

Test suites. Required evidence on every PR that touches the matching surface.

  • Unit (Mocha)
  • Integration (Mocha)
  • Webview contract (Playwright)
  • Fixtures
prompts/

Curated model prompts used at runtime.

  • Selection-scoped edit prompt

Operations

Workflows, infrastructure, and helpers that automate the lifecycle and ship the product.

.github/

Lifecycle automation and contributor guardrails.

  • Agentic workflows
  • Deterministic workflows
  • Shared workflow fragments
  • PR and issue templates
  • Copilot instructions
infra/

Azure infrastructure for monitoring. Deployed by the release stage.

  • Monitoring Bicep
  • Generated alert templates
  • Action group definitions
scripts/

Build and dev-loop helpers.

  • Extension bundler
  • Dev host launcher
tools/

Deterministic tooling that backs lifecycle pipelines.

  • Monitoring pipeline tools
  • Release verifier

Documentation surfaces

Where the harness publishes outward-facing context for users, contributors, and reviewers.

docs/external/

Public GitHub Pages content.

  • Engineering lifecycle page (this doc)
  • Scenario traceability matrix
docs/internal/

Contributor-only notes that must stay out of the Marketplace README.

  • Contributor setup and workflow notes
Root

Marketplace-public surfaces. Treated as user-facing copy, not contributor docs.

  • README.md
  • CHANGELOG.md
  • LICENSE
